chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymi, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from al-Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The body is built upon bread.
ai.seo_question: What is the primary sustenance of the human body according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this concise hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Jafar al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies bread as the foundational sustenance of the human body, reflecting the dietary norms of the early Islamic period. This statement underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the physical vessel as a trust (*amanah*) that requires basic nourishment to function, linking material needs to spiritual discipline. It serves as a reminder that while the body is hollow and dependent on food, its proper maintenance is a prerequisite for fulfilling one's religious and worldly duties.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ali Bin Al Hassan Al Taymi, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Biin Hakeym, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, from Al Waleed Bin Sabeeh, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘But rather, the body is built upon the bread’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ali ibn af-Hassan al-Tamimiy from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad Hakim from Ibrahim ibn ‘Abd al- Hamid from af-Wafid ibn Sabih who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The body is made out of bread (food).”’
